listingTitle: Release synchronous Rust locks before await
title: Release synchronous Rust locks before await
why: Holding a synchronous mutex guard across await can block an executor worker and deadlock tasks that need the same lock.
suggestion: Limit the guard to an inner scope before awaiting, or use an async-aware mutex when the guard must span a yield point.
limitations: Direct, optionally multiline lock-guard bindings on identifier or field receivers that unwrap a lock result or use parking_lot inside async code are recognized. Dereferenced copies and results extracted through another call are not guard bindings.
Only awaits in the guard's enclosing lexical block and outside nested async bodies count as suspension points; the same source guard is reported once.

Type aliases, custom synchronous lock APIs, borrowed guard bindings, arbitrary receiver expressions, data-flow moves, and implicit early drops are not resolved. Explicit drop and nested lexical block boundaries are recognized.
